key_insight: KNIGHT combines topic-specific knowledge graphs with LLM generation and an adaptive hardness calibration to produce controllable, high-quality multiple-choice questions at scale for evaluating RAG and other LLM systems.
problem_solved: Building specialized MCQ assessment datasets for evaluating LLMs and RAG systems is time-consuming and costly. KNIGHT automates dataset creation while providing fine-grained control over question difficulty and provenance.
method: Construct a topic-specific knowledge graph from external sources to create a structured, concise representation of entities and relations.
Use the KG as structured context to prompt an LLM to generate question stems, a correct answer, and plausible distractors with provenance links.
Apply adaptive hardness calibration—score difficulty, select/adjust distractors, and iteratively refine questions—to produce a targeted distribution of easy/medium/hard MCQs.
impact: Enables scalable, cost-effective generation of MCQ benchmarks with controllable difficulty and traceable provenance, improving the robustness and speed of LLM/RAG evaluation and dataset creation workflows.

paper_title: KNIGHT: Knowledge Graph-Driven Multiple-Choice Question Generation with Adaptive Hardness Calibration
